mt_cascade_creek.blurb: Cascade Creek is a bouldering area in Gallatin Canyon, Montana, found by leaving the Lava Lake trail and crossing the creek. The boulders are large blocks of gneiss scattered through talus on the canyon's south side, in an alpine, forested setting with moss and lichen underfoot. Every climb here is a boulder problem, just over a hundred of them, running from V0 to V10 with most between V3 and V7. Explosive Area holds the most climbs, followed by Carpenter Boulder, Lava Pit and Behind the Curtain, each with around a dozen problems.

nv_carson_city_area.blurb: Carson City Area is a cluster of climbing spots in western Nevada that leans toward bouldering, with sport and trad routes making up the rest. Boulder problems run from V0 to V10, mostly V0 to V3, while roped climbs run roughly 5.6 to 5.12, most between 5.9 and 5.11. Washoe Boulders holds the most climbs, on volcanic rock that is hard on the fingers, and it can be climbed year round although summers get very hot. Prison Hill is desert volcanic rock with pockets, crimps and huecos, mostly boulder problems and sport routes, and it is good in winter. Dinosaur Rock is mainly trad, and The Book of Red is mainly sport.

tn_the_canyon_at_pond_creek.blurb: The Canyon at Pond Creek is a sport-focused crag in Tennessee's Sequatchie Valley, about fifty minutes from Chattanooga. It holds a little over a hundred routes, mostly sport with a smaller group of trad lines, ranging from 5.6 to 5.13 with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.13. The sandstone is very hard, and the lines include steep roofs, an offwidth chimney and arete climbs. Tiger Wall holds the most climbs, followed by The Den, The Right Side and Early Bird Wall. At The Right Side the climbing is mostly moderate sport, roughly 5.8 to 5.11, with some trad as well.

tx_hamm_creek_park.blurb: Hamm Creek Park in Texas spreads its climbing over a few areas: Carrion Wall and Indian Head, Bailey Hollow and Hostility Boulders. Sport routes make up most of it, with a set of boulder problems and a few trad lines, mostly 5.9 to 5.11 on the rope and V0 to V4 on the boulders. The rock is on the chossy side and holds can break, although some spots are more solid. In Bailey Hollow the main boulder sits on notably solid limestone, and the boulders at Old Bailey stand in shade through the year under large cottonwoods and oaks, kept cool by wind off the river.

wi_4_group_camp_b.blurb: Group Camp B is a bouldering area in Governor Dodge State Park in southern Wisconsin, with just over a hundred problems and a single top rope. The stone is hard grey sandstone in big, separate blocks and short walls. Most lines are close to vertical, with a few shorter, steeper ones, and the holds are pockets, crimps, slopers and pinches. Plenty of highballs make some problems feel closer to a route. Grades run from V0 to V8, mostly V0 to V4. Backbone Ridge, a ridge jutting off the hilltop with problems on both sides, holds the most climbs, and Plan B Area adds boulders and a small wall. The east side of the ridge is mostly shaded.

ab_radium_highway_93_south.blurb: Radium Highway (93 South) is a string of ice, mixed and sport crags reached along Highway 93 south of Castle Junction. Stanley Headwall holds the most climbs: its routes are sustained multi-pitch ice and mixed lines, roughly WI3 to WI6 and up to M8, typically three to seven pitches, and a rock section there is mostly sport. Haffner Creek is mostly mixed, M5 to M8 and harder, with some ice and a few sport and trad routes. Castleview, Storm Creek Headwall and Marble Canyon add more. The rock routes run about 5.7 to 5.13, concentrated between 5.10 and 5.12.
